channel.title: Personal News Feed — Technology & Science
channel.description: Personally scored technology & science articles curated by news-filter

item.title: 1Password reports backend breach following compromise of employee GitHub account
item.description:
Source: The Verge, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, PCWorld, PCMag Original headline: 1Password Reports Backend Breach Following Compromised Employee GitHub Account
1Password confirmed a security incident that began on November 19 when an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account. The attacker used this access to reach source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing for the download of administrative data. Stolen information includes customer names, email addresses, account and user identifiers, and certain non-secret internal metadata. The breach also involved private source code, the company's CI/CD system, and certain tokens from emailed invitation, provisioning, or account recovery links. 1Password maintains that customer password vaults and the keys used to protect them remain secure, and there is no evidence of actual account takeovers. To mitigate the breach, the company disabled the affected GitHub account, rotated or revoked potentially exposed internal credentials, and added a new detection system. Additionally, 1Password lengthened emailed codes from six digits to a 10-character alphanumeric string to prevent guessing. Users are advised to remain vigilant against phishing attempts, as names and emails were part of the leaked data.
item.source: The Verge, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, PCWorld, PCMag

item.title: Todoist hacker accesses production systems and steals credentials for 6 percent of customers
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, PCMag Original headline: Todoist Data Breach Affects 6% of Customers via Stolen Credentials
A hacker gained access to Todoist production systems between November 22 and November 23, affecting approximately 6% of the company's customer base. The attacker used stolen credentials to access the version control system and source code, eventually reaching the cloud infrastructure through an employee's work account. The breach specifically targeted early users whose passwords used an older salted SHA1 hashing method. While the hacker downloaded email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates, there was no indication that the attacker signed in to those specific accounts. For a subset of 0.001% of users, the hacker searched tasks, comments, and attachment names for API keys and access tokens, as well as Slack integration tokens. If the Todoist for Outlook extension was active, the hacker could potentially access emails, addresses, and attachment file names. Todoist has blocked the attack path, reset internal access structures, and disabled the Outlook email add-on. CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized for the incident, stating the company will investigate why it happened. Affected users are advised to reset credentials and update API tokens or integrations.

item.title: Apple will not bring macOS to iPad or merge operating systems
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple has tested macOS on iPads internally, but won’t release it to consumers
Apple has internally tested macOS on iPad hardware, but the company will not release the desktop operating system to consumers or merge iPadOS and macOS into a single platform. Bloomberg journalist Mark Gurman states there is no current work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad. While the shared silicon architecture makes running macOS on iPad hardware technically feasible, Apple intends to instead bring individual Mac capabilities and professional applications, such as Final Cut, to iPadOS over time. Regulatory pressures from the European Union, which evaluates compliance on a per-operating-system basis, provide an incentive to keep the platforms separate. Software chief Craig Federighi previously noted that putting macOS directly onto an iPad would undermine the tablet's distinct nature, a sentiment echoed by CEO John Ternus. Instead of a full OS replacement, Apple is focusing on expanding multitasking and desktop-style controls, such as windowing and menu bars, within iPadOS while maintaining touch-first usability.

item.title: Microsoft reduces Windows 11 memory usage through service and resource optimizations
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Your Windows 11 PC is getting a speed boost thanks to major RAM cuts
Microsoft is reducing memory usage in Windows 11 to improve system performance. At the Ignite developer conference, the company announced that the Defender security program, OneDrive cloud storage, and the Purview data protection service now collectively use over 500 MB less RAM. Additionally, memory usage in Microsoft 365 has been reduced by 360 MB. These optimizations involve reviewing which components must be loaded into RAM and determining how different components can share resources. Microsoft is prioritizing these improvements to assist computers equipped with 8 or 16 GB of RAM due to rising memory prices, though users with higher-capacity hardware will also see benefits. Some of these memory-saving improvements have already been released as part of the Windows 11 October update.

item.title: Army detonates lead azide stockpile in Iowa without detecting airborne lead
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Ars Technica Original headline: Army detonates remaining lead azide stockpile in Iowa with no detected airborne lead
The US Army detonated 68 barrels containing approximately 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning. The controlled explosion, involving two earth-covered containers detonated simultaneously, was necessary because the compound had become unstable due to crystallization. To prevent the release of lead, a neurotoxin, the Army used water tanks, tarps, containment screens, and foam to capture particulates. While smoke plumes reached several hundred feet, the US Environmental Protection Agency reported that real-time air monitors detected zero airborne lead in the region one hour after the blast. Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley stated the operation reduced health and safety risks to Middletown and surrounding communities as close to zero as possible. As a precaution, FEMA supported a voluntary temporary relocation for residents within a five-mile cone-shaped evacuation zone, with some scheduled to remain lodged until Friday, November 27th. Other residents were advised to shelter in place by closing windows and doors.

item.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit despite software malfunction during propulsion operation
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: The latest ESA mission to Mercury was nearly derailed by a last-minute 'software issue'
The BepiColombo spacecraft, a joint project by the European and Japanese space agencies, has successfully entered orbit around Mercury despite a software malfunction during its arrival. The European Space Agency confirmed that a software issue caused a thruster burn that was shorter than planned during the orbital insertion. While the spacecraft remains safe, engineers are investigating the malfunction before scientific operations proceed. This mission follows a difficult trajectory involving one Earth encounter, two Venus encounters, and six passages around Mercury to manage the planet's high speed. Previous propulsion difficulties in 2024 had already delayed the expected arrival from mid-2025 to November 2026. BepiColombo carries two orbiters: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter, which will study surface materials and magnetic conditions, and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which will focus on the magnetic environment and plasma. Scientific investigations are expected to begin in April 2027. The mission must operate under intense thermal exposure, as Mercury receives ten times the sunlight that reaches Earth.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Leak details specifications for seven new Intel Nova Lake-S desktop processors
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: 7 new Intel Nova Lake-S Core Ultra 4000-series CPUs detailed in new leak
A leaked document details seven new Intel Nova Lake-S Core Ultra 4000-series desktop processors based on C1 stepping qualification samples. The leak, reported by VideoCardz, includes a top-of-the-line Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC featuring 28 cores, including eight performance, 16 efficiency, and four low-power efficient cores. This chip reportedly reaches a 5.5 GHz boost speed with 144 MB of L3 cache and a 125-watt power rating. Other leaked models include a Core Ultra 9 4950K, a 22-core Core 9 4900 BFC, mid-range Core Ultra 7 4870K and 4850K chips, and entry-level Core Ultra 5 4650K and 4650KF models. All seven processors reportedly support DDR5-8000 RAM, a maximum of 256 GB of RAM, 24 PCIe lanes, and a 77 PTOPS integrated NPU. While a previous report suggested Nova Lake chips might limit maximum core frequency to 5.1 GHz when exceeding 90°C, this limitation only applies if those temperatures are reached. Intel may announce these chips in Berlin, Germany, between February 22 and 25, 2026.

item.title: Hera spacecraft reveals crater on Dimorphos caused by NASA asteroid deflection test
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Engadget Original headline: Hera spacecraft reveals damage caused by NASA's asteroid deflection experiment
The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has captured images of a crater the size of a sports stadium on the asteroid Dimorphos. This damage resulted from NASA’s September 2022 Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART), a mission that released 10 billion joules of energy upon impact at speeds exceeding 13,700 mph. While the impact successfully shortened Dimorphos’s orbit around its companion, Didymos, by 33 minutes, Hera revealed that the impact also sent the asteroid tumbling and that the crater extends across the entire width of the 500-foot-wide rock. Principal investigator Patrick Michel noted that the crater did not alter the fields of boulders covering the rest of the asteroid. Mission manager Ian Carnelli stated that combining these missions allows humanity to make asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting Earth. In December, ESA plans to move Hera closer for higher-resolution images, and in January, the mission will deploy CubeSats, including the Juventas and Milani, to probe the asteroid's interior and prospect surrounding materials.

item.title: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messaging for text, photos, and videos
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends, Engadget, TechCrunch Original headline: WhatsApp introduces scheduled messaging for text, photos, and videos
WhatsApp is rolling out a scheduled messaging feature to its 3 billion users on iOS and Android over the coming weeks. The update allows users to schedule text, photos, and videos to be sent anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days in the future. To use the tool, a user writes a message and long-presses the send button to select a delivery time. Scheduled messages maintain end-to-end encryption and will be delivered even if the sender's phone is powered off or out of battery at the scheduled time. Users can manage or delete pending messages via a list, though they cannot currently edit a message once it has been scheduled. In group chats, scheduled messages only reach members who were part of the group when the message was written. The feature is currently unavailable for WhatsApp Business accounts. While competitors like Telegram and Signal already offer scheduling, WhatsApp intends for this tool to help users coordinate across time zones and send timely reminders.
item.source: The Verge, Digital Trends, Engadget, TechCrunch

item.title: Allstate technical outage disrupts website and mobile app services nationwide
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: Allstate Nationwide Tech Outage Disrupts Services Ahead of Thanksgiving
Allstate is facing a nationwide technical outage affecting its website and mobile app, preventing customers from accessing accounts, filing claims, or paying bills. Users began reporting disruptions on Monday morning, according to Downdetector. While a formal cause or resolution time has not been issued, Allstate advised that customers will not lose coverage or incur late fees if the interruption impacts payments. An employee at a California office confirmed that staff are processing inbound calls but cannot access actual policies, and noted that email access has been inconsistent. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN that as companies patch digital infrastructure, Americans should expect certain "glitches, gaps, [and] interruptions in service." This instability follows reports that Allstate may lay off up to 10% of its staff, or roughly 5,000 employees, as part of an AI-driven efficiency push. During a November 5 earnings call, CEO Tom Wilson discussed the upcoming launch of personal agentic assistants, such as Muse, Spark, and Dot, to handle consumer transactions.

item.title: WhatsApp tests sound-enabled stickers for beta users
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp Tests New Feature Allowing Sound-Enabled Stickers
WhatsApp is testing a new feature that allows beta users to create and send stickers with audio. Currently being rolled out to select Android and iOS beta testers, the tool enables users to convert a video into an animated sticker and attach a sound. Users can choose to keep the original video audio, record a voice note lasting up to 5 seconds, or select a custom audio file or built-in sound effect such as 'Cat Purr' or 'Crickets.' This functionality could allow for the recreation of internet memes like the Josh Hutcherson 'Whistle' edit. To prevent noise in group chats, stickers arrive muted, and recipients must tap an audio icon to hear the sound, which loops three times before stopping. End-to-end encryption protects both the animation and the audio. WhatsApp has not yet announced a release date for the general public.

item.title: Google Docs adds direct Word file support to Compare documents tool
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google adds Word file support to the Compare documents tool in Docs
Google Docs now allows users to compare a Word (.docx) file directly without requiring a prior conversion. Previously, the Compare documents tool under the Tools menu only supported native Google Docs files, forcing teams to convert Word documents to compare amendments. Google Workspace engineering lead Chandu Thota stated that .docx files can now be compared directly, which should reduce the number of converted file versions stored in Google Drive. When using the tool, Docs generates a fresh comparison document showing amendments as proposed edits, and comments can also be transferred from the Word document. This process does not affect either of the original files. The functionality is automatically enabled when a .docx file is opened in Docs and is available to all Workspace customers, Workspace Individual sign-ups, and personal Google account holders. The update has already rolled out to both Rapid Release and Scheduled Release environments.

item.title: PROFILE: Eunice Wang argues AI consumer products require clear purpose and meaningful user experiences
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: For CES Judge Eunice Wang, Creative Experimentation Offers Signals for AI’s Consumer Future
Eunice Wang, founder of WHAT NOW STUDIOS, has completed her service as a judge for the CES Innovation Awards 2027 program. Wang argues that for AI consumer products to succeed, they must offer a clearly defined role in daily life by making a specific experience meaningfully better. She notes that a device's physical form and interaction matter as much as its software capabilities. To illustrate this, Wang's studio worked with MARK, an AI bookmark for physical books, and served as a launch partner for Blinkko, a wearable AI companion. Beyond consumer hardware, Wang monitors creative experimentation as a source of signals for future products, including AI-assisted creative processes and digitally fabricated objects like 3D-printed clothing. Her studio also hosts programming such as the November 14 Creators Connect Artist Salon, which featured Corin Roddick of Purity Ring. Wang maintains that any experimental idea must eventually be tested for practical use, requiring a clear activity to support and a reason for users to return to the experience.

item.title: Nothing announces Ear (note) earbuds with AI transcription and summarization capabilities
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Nothing announces Ear (note) AI-enabled earbuds with built-in notetaking
Nothing has announced the Ear (note), a pair of AI-enabled wireless earbuds scheduled to launch on December 8. Designed as a personal productivity tool, the device can transcribe and summarize in-person conversations, calls, online meetings, and voice memos. The charging case records face-to-face meetings, while the earbuds capture phone calls, with a companion app providing transcriptions and AI-generated summaries. The aluminum charging case features physical controls, including a large Talk button for recording, a smaller button marked with a red dot, and status lights. Nothing plans to support various AI agents, including a proprietary voice-control system for back-and-forth conversations. While the company has not released specific pricing or technical specifications, it promised the device will support Hi-Res audio and offer its best in-ear audio experience to date. Nothing stated that steps have been taken to address privacy concerns regarding the device's recording capabilities.

item.title: Ladybird releases first downloadable alpha browser engine built from scratch
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
The Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, providing prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, users had to compile the browser from source, but the new version provides an installable package with automatic updating. Unlike Chrome, Edge, or Firefox, Ladybird is not a browser fork; its rendering engine and LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. Project lead Andreas Kling stated, "The engine is our our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork. The browser around it is modest, but functional." The project, which originated from Kling's SerenityOS project, is managed by the Ladybird Browser Initiative, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by sponsorships and donations. Because it lacks sponsored search engine deals, sponsoring entities have no influence over the project roadmap. While unlikely to shift market tides immediately, the new engine provides an independent implementation of web standards that can reveal where websites depend on Chromium-specific behaviors rather than published specifications.

item.title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down next week
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down next week amid IPO uncertainty
Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down next week, with his last day scheduled for December 4. Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan will lead the company until a successor is named in the coming weeks. Krishnamurthy, who joined the company in 2015 and became CEO in 2017, oversaw a period where business grew more than five-fold and managed the company through Walmart’s $16 billion acquisition in 2018. Under his leadership, Flipkart grew to include over 500 million registered users and expanded into quick-commerce and food delivery. This leadership change occurs amid uncertainty regarding a planned initial public offering. While Flipkart moved its headquarters from Singapore to India in March to prepare for a public listing, Walmart reportedly advised the company in May to delay the IPO to focus on profitability. Walmart International president and CEO Chris Nicholas stated, "Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan."

item.title: Google adds images, stopwatch, and reminders to Gemini Notebook flashcards
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google Gemini Notebook upgrades Flashcards with visual learning and study reminders
Google is adding visual learning and scheduling tools to the Flashcards feature in Gemini Notebook. The update allows the tool to automatically pull relevant images, such as anatomy diagrams or maps, directly from uploaded study materials and place them alongside text on flashcards. To assist with exam preparation, Google is also adding a built-in stopwatch that lets users track how long they spend reviewing material to improve recall speed. Additionally, the Gemini Notebook mobile app will now include scheduled study reminders, allowing users to set notifications to revisit previously generated flashcards. These updates follow the initial introduction of Flashcards and customizable quizzes in September 2025. The new features are currently available to personal Google accounts, Google Workspace customers, and Workspace Individual subscribers without requiring a paid AI subscription.

item.title: Kagi launches private email and calendar service as Gmail alternative
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
Palo Alto-based software company Kagi has launched Kagi Mail, a subscription-based email service and calendar intended to rival Gmail. Currently in public beta, the web-only service emphasizes privacy, personal data sovereignty, and an ad-free experience. Features include 50GB of storage, unlimited aliases and domains, rule-based filtering with Sieve, and optional AI tools for searching email history and re-labeling. While native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year, a contacts address book will not arrive until the first quarter of 2027. Kagi Mail is included in the $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription, which also provides frontier AI models. Alternatively, users can subscribe to the mail service separately for $9 per month or $99 per year, with a 60-day trial currently available. This move follows Kagi's existing business model as a subscription-based alternative to Google's search engine.

item.title: Seabirds with audio recorders detect commercial vessels missing from public tracking systems
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Seabirds With Audio Recorders Are Hunting Down Unseen Ships—and Finding More Than Expected
Seabirds equipped with lightweight audio recorders can detect commercial vessels that evade public tracking systems, according to a study published in Science Advances. Lead author Jonathan Rutter, a postdoctoral research fellow at the University of Oxford, notes that while many ships use the automatic identification system (AIS) to broadcast location and speed, a significant portion of industrial fishing and transport vessels go undetected. By attaching recorders and GPS trackers to northern gannets, Balearic shearwaters, and Westland petrels, researchers identified low-frequency engine hums that reveal the presence of unseen ships. In one instance, northern gannets spent an average of 68 minutes per day near ships, but at least 22 minutes of that time involved vessels not detected by AIS. This means at least 32% of vessel audio captured by gannets came from undetected vessels, though researchers suggest the true proportion may be closer to 57%. This method helps fill data gaps in the footprints of risk that guide marine conservation and help protect seabird populations from fishing gear.

item.title: Mexican hairy dwarf porcupine glows in neon colors under ultraviolet light
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Mexico’s Nocturnal Porcupine Has Been Keeping a Secret. It Glows in Neon Colors Under UV Light
Wildlife veterinarian Jonathan Pérez-Flores and colleagues report that the Mexican hairy dwarf porcupine (Coendou mexicanus) exhibits photoluminescence, glowing in shades of blue, green, and yellow under ultraviolet (UV) light. In a study published this November in Neotropical Biology and Conservation, researchers tested 20 live adult porcupines and two preserved museum specimens. While all subjects exhibited photoluminescence, live animals displayed greater intensity and a wider range of colors than the museum specimens. Because these nocturnal animals live in dense tree cover and hide in hollows during the day, they are often missed by standard forest-floor camera traps. Researchers suggest that using simple, consumer-grade LED UV flashlights could serve as a useful tool for locating and conducting nighttime censuses of these populations in the wild. While the ecological purpose of this trait remains unknown, the team intends to investigate whether the species possesses the biological pigments or retinal cones necessary to detect UV light, and whether the glowing quills aid in communication, mimicry, or camouflage.

item.title: SALES: RoboForm for Business enables secure credential sharing and granular permission management
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: How RoboForm for Business Helps Teams Share Logins Safely
RoboForm for Business provides a secure alternative to sharing passwords via spreadsheets, emails, or text messages, which can lead to security breaches and loss of control. The platform allows administrators to manage employee access through a central Admin Center, where they can set company security policies, onboard users, and manage secure data. To ensure accountability, the tool provides reports and audit logs to track activity. Permissions can be managed granularly through company groups. Limited users can autofill shared logins without viewing or editing credentials, while Regular users can update shared credentials, and Group Managers can manage membership and permissions. The service supports integration with major identity providers, including Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace, Ping, and OneLogin, and offers on-premises Microsoft Active Directory support for synchronizing users and groups. Administrators can also connect supported single sign-on (SSO) and system for cross-domain identity management (SCIM) software to streamline user provisioning.

item.title: Neuralink receives FDA approval for brain implant trial in ALS patients
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Neuralink receives FDA approval for 'pivotal' brain implant trial in ALS patients
Neuralink has received FDA permission to launch a pivotal trial for its LINK implantable brain-computer interface. The study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of the device, specifically focusing on whether patients can use thought to control digital devices and improve independence in daily life. The trial will be open to a limited number of patients with ALS, a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that damages nerve cells responsible for voluntary muscle movement. This follows previous work involving more than 30 participants. Last year, participant Bradford Smith demonstrated the ability to communicate using brain signals alone, stating that the technology provided him with freedom and faster communication. The LINK system involves surgically placing an N1 implant in the skull, using an R1 robot to insert flexible electrodes into the brain. Software then interprets brain activity associated with movement to translate signals into commands for digital devices. If the technology proves safe and reliable, the trial may lead to further clinical trials and eventual market release.

item.title: Backblaze privacy policy change allows sharing certain personal data with advertisers
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
Backblaze will implement a new privacy policy on December 1 that allows the cloud storage company to share certain personal information with advertising and marketing partners. Under the current policy, Backblaze does not share email or physical addresses for marketing purposes without user consent, nor does it mention advertisers. The new policy includes a table of general personal information that may be shared, such as names, email addresses, IP addresses, commercial purchasing histories, and geolocation data. The new policy also lists sensory or surveillance data, including call recordings or other audio and visual monitoring, as part of the information collected. However, a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that the company does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and does not disclose such data to advertising or marketing partners.

item.title: SALES: ASUS provides liquid cooling options ranging from budget builds to enthusiast flagship models
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: From budget builds to gaming beasts, ASUS has an AIO cooler for every kind of PC build
ASUS offers a range of all-in-one (AIO) liquid coolers designed for different PC building needs, ranging from budget-friendly options to high-end enthusiast models. While air cooling is simple and custom liquid loops offer maximum flexibility, AIOs provide a preassembled, sealed middle ground that balances performance and convenience. Upgrading to an AIO can help maintain stable temperatures during heavy workloads, such as gaming or rendering, and can free up space around the CPU socket. ASUS's lineup includes the LC 360 ARGB, which provides essential cooling and daisy-chained fans for easier cable management. The TUF Gaming LC III series offers practical cooling with optional LCD displays for hardware monitoring. For premium builds, the ROG Strix LC III series utilizes an Asetek Gen7 V2 pump and a 2.1-inch IPS screen. Flagship models like the ROG Ryujin III and Ryuo IV target enthusiasts, featuring advanced pumps and large displays, including a 6.67-inch curved AMOLED screen on the Ryuo IV.

item.title: Insta360 schedules Ace Pro 3 camera reveal for December 1
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Insta360 teases the Ace Pro 3 action camera ahead of its December 1 launch
Insta360 has announced that it will reveal details regarding its upcoming Ace Pro 3 action camera during a launch event on December 1. The company shared a teaser for the device on its official Weibo account and on X, though it has not yet confirmed a price, a global availability window, or a full specification sheet. While specific technical details remain unconfirmed, the teaser suggests the Ace Pro 3 may support variable aperture and swappable lenses. The current Ace Pro 2 features an 8K resolution and a Leica lens, but these specifications are not confirmed for the new model. To build interest, Insta360 is hosting a giveaway where fans who follow and repost on Weibo can enter for a chance to win an Ace Pro 3 on December 24. The announcement comes during a competitive year for the action camera market, which includes products such as the GoPro Hero 13 Black and DJI's Osmo Action cameras.

item.title: Enough Phone increases battery, storage, and RAM specifications before market release
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The tiny Enough Phone gets a much-needed specs bump as it nears market release
The Enough Phone is increasing several hardware specifications as it nears its official market release. The device, which features a small screen and pocketable form factor, will now include a 3,700mAh battery using silicon-carbon chemistry, up from the previously advertised 3,500mAh. Storage capacity has also increased from 128GB to 256GB, and RAM has been upgraded from 8GB to 12GB. These hardware changes aim to meet the demands of apps with increasing AI integrations without increasing the retail price. The project is currently roughly 85% funded and requires 100 more backers to reach its goal. The team anticipates shipping costs will be $8 for domestic US orders and $30 for international shipping, excluding customs fees.

item.title: Razer and Durex partner for limited-edition mousepad and condom kit in China
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Razer China partners up with Durex for a limited-edition kit of mousepad and condoms
Razer has partnered with Durex in China to release a limited-edition kit containing a Razer Goliath mousepad and two Razer-branded Durex Performa delay condoms. The kit is available through Razer or Durex stores on JD.com, or via Tmall's Durex store through point redemption and live-stream events. A giveaway is scheduled for Dec. 7. The promotion uses wordplay involving the heavy armored beetle mousepad and the long-lasting battle armor condom variant, which both share a way of referring to armor or shells in Chinese. The partnership's slogan is "for gaming, bring Razer; for romance, bring Durex." While the pairing may seem unusual, Durex has sponsored the Chinese League of Legends Pro League since 2023. Razer has previously engaged in unconventional collaborations with brands such as Gillette, Panerai, and Dolce & Gabbana. Market reports suggest the younger Chinese demographic is open to such unconventional branding pairings.

item.title: Iranian hacking unit targets French refrigeration systems and critical infrastructure
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
The Shahid Kaveh hacking unit, an elite wing of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, targeted commercial refrigeration systems in France last October, destroying millions of euros worth of food. French intelligence agencies identified traces of Farsi in the digital trail, linking the attack to the group, which also operates under the persona CyberAv3ngers. This unit has a history of targeting critical infrastructure, including hacking Israeli-made industrial control devices in water, manufacturing, and transportation systems across several US states in 2023 and 2024. In those instances, the group declared, “Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.” Experts view the targeting of European infrastructure as an escalation in Iran's cyber warfare strategy. Ellie Geranmayeh of the European Council on Foreign Relations says Iran has messaged that the global economy will face disruption as a consequence of the country being shut out from the world.

item.title: Visual effects supervisor used lava bible to create ring-forging scene in Rings of Power
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: ‘Rings of Power’ Had a ‘Lava Bible’ to Help Bring the Ring-Forging Scene to Life
In season three of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, the character Sauron, played by Charlie Vickers, crafts the One Ring using heat from Mount Doom and guidance from the Balrog, voiced by Simon Pegg. Visual effects supervisor Jason Smith called the ring-forging sequence the hardest he has pulled off in a 25-year career. To ensure a realistic appearance, Smith and his team studied real volcanic eruptions and created a "lava bible" containing different flavors of lava and specific actions. This guide used keywords like "burblers" and "geysers" to direct the visual effects. Smith also used color variations in the flames to communicate extreme heat to the audience. Vickers received glimpses of the visual effects between takes to help ground his performance during what he called "arguably the moment in the Tolkien legendarium." While season three concludes with this sequence, a fourth season is officially in development.
